33.text: CAMPS AND VILLAGES. — The camps of the Reindeer Chukchee are situated

34.text: in groups, mostly along the rivers; and their grazing-grounds are divided by

35.text: watersheds, which are ordinarily so devoid of vegetation and so exposed to

36.text: winds as to be unfit for reindeer-breeding. In the fall the camps are moved

37.text: to the border of the forest to find shelter from the winter tempests; while in

38.text: the spring of the year the herds are driven to the tundra, as far as the sea-

39.text: coast, in order to be freer from noxious insects, and to give them pasturage

40.text: better suited for the summer season. Some of the camps near the head waters

41.text: of several rivers move to the mountains instead of to the sea, and stay near

42.text: some small glacier, where the insects are less numerous than in the valleys.

43.text: Often these herds do not thrive so well as those which are driven down to

44.text: the sea. The range of the wanderings of a Chukchee camp extends from a

45.text: hundred to a hundred and fifty miles, and in most cases covers the same or

46.text: nearly the same territory every year; but any camp that becomes dissatisfied

47.text: with its range may pick out a new one wherever it chooses, the only condition
